items.title: Cybernetics and Ghosts
items.summary: A short, sharp reading of Italo Calvino's 1967 lecture on whether machines could replace writers — Calvino argued that once algorithms expose all of writing's rules, authors are finally free to break them deliberately and find something genuinely original.
items.why: Reframes the AI-versus-creativity debate through a 60-year-old lens that holds up better than most 2026 takes — useful clarity for a design lead thinking about what in their team's practice is actually irreplaceable when AI can generate competent output on demand.

items.title: How tech's most craft-obsessed team uses AI: Inside design at Linear
items.summary: A case study on how Linear's design team deliberately caps AI use at 20–30% of new work, built a custom tool trained on their design philosophy to argue against their own proposals, and treats the decision of what not to automate as the core design judgment.
items.why: The countercultural takeaway — 'when you can do anything, what you choose not to do matters most' — is directly relevant to how Manik thinks about AI adoption inside CueDesign: the question isn't which tools to add but what to protect from them.

items.title: The branding challenge behind Mayor Zohran's new municipal grocery stores
items.summary: Elizabeth Goodspeed unpacks the open brief to brand NYC Groceries — five city-owned stores across all five boroughs — asking what civic branding should actually do when public trust is the goal rather than commercial aspiration or competitive positioning.
items.why: The civic-versus-commercial branding problem ('all the clout, none of the baggage') maps onto how Cuemath earns credibility with parents and students: brand that signals safety and learning, not sales — a constraint Goodspeed articulates more sharply than most brand strategy writing.

items.title: New Contemporaries 2026
items.summary: Ashley Kinnard Studio's exhibition book for South London Gallery pairs two typefaces — expressive Artistik and stable Zénith (205TF) — as an A-to-Z structure, with letters replacing page numbers and 26 artists each contributing one entry to a shared visual vocabulary.
items.why: A clean example of typographic system design that carries the full conceptual weight of a publication — the structural thinking (one rule, applied consistently, does all the heavy lifting) translates directly to design systems work.
